Class.summary: Controller responsible for managing communication, notes, and discussion comments on support tickets.
Class.remarks: Route prefix: api/v1/tickets/{ticketId}/comments. All comment endpoints require authentication and enforce ticket-level ownership access control.

Constructor.summary: Initializes a new instance of the class.
Constructor.param: The MediatR mediator instance used for dispatching comment queries and commands.
The service used to obtain the current authenticated user's ID and role from JWT claims.

GetComments.summary: Retrieves the chronological discussion thread of comments for a specific support ticket.
GetComments.remarks: Access is governed by ticket ownership rules: Admin: Can view comments on any ticket in the system. SupportAgent: Can view comments on tickets assigned to them. Customer: Can view comments on tickets they created. Comments are returned ordered chronologically by creation timestamp (CreatedAt ascending).
GetComments.param: The unique identifier (GUID) of the parent ticket.
GetComments.returns: A list of comment response DTOs including author display name, comment content, and creation timestamp.
GetComments.response: Returns the chronological list of comments for the ticket.
If the provided ticket ID is not a valid GUID format.
If the request lacks a valid Bearer token.
If the ticket does not exist or the caller lacks permission to view it.

AddComment.summary: Posts a new comment to a support ticket thread.
AddComment.remarks: Authorized for users with access to the ticket: Administrators, the assigned Support Agent, or the ticket owner Customer. Content Limits: Content cannot be blank and must not exceed 2000 characters. Posting a comment automatically logs a CommentAdded activity event in the ticket timeline.
AddComment.param: The unique identifier (GUID) of the parent ticket.
The comment payload containing the text content to post.
AddComment.returns: A confirmation response indicating the comment was added successfully.
AddComment.response: If the comment payload fails validation (e.g., blank content or text exceeding 2000 characters).
If the request lacks a valid Bearer token.
If the ticket does not exist or the caller lacks permission to post comments to it.
